articleTitle: Domain-Specific Software System Testing by Using Intelligent Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: As Software industries have grown over the last few years, software testing has been considered a crucial process in the software development lifecycle. In the past, software testing was done manually, and this is a very laborious and costly process that carries errors and requires time, money, and effort. Currently, testers want to perform the testing automatically to save time and get accurate results. In this paper, we propose the development of a domain-specific tool Architecture to automate test case generation across various industries like Automotive, Finance, and healthcare. This will retrieve user requirements and apply Intelligent Techniques to generate test cases. By enhancing the intelligent models' concrete tests with fewer ambiguities can be generated through this tool.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Misbehavior Detection in Intelligent Transportation Systems Using BSM Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Vehicular networks focus on improving traffic and safety concerns in an Intelligent Transportation System (ITS). However, the presence of misbehaving nodes can drastically impact the safety, traffic and other applications offered by ITS. Misbehavior detection forms an important mechanism in an ITS to detect and mitigate the effect of misbehaving nodes. The proposed work focuses on analyzing the performance of popular machine learning algorithms for misbehavior detection in VANETs. The effect on performance pre and post-regulation is also highlighted. VEREMI dataset is used as the dataset of choice for the analysis

articleTitle: Smart Expiry Tracker and Product Recommender using Google ML Kit OCR Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Expiration dates play a crucial role in both personal and business contexts, influencing everything from health man-agement to operational efficiency. Track Expiry Dates (TED) is a comprehensive mobile application designed to address two key needs: document management and expiry tracking. We designed a secure app which offers users to store personal documents such as driving licenses, passports, general documents, product warranty cards, and bills, ensuring that critical information is readily accessible and safeguarded against loss or damage. The proposed system provides a seamless and efficient solution for tracking expiry dates and storing essential documents such as Aadhar cards and PAN cards. It automatically sends reminders to users and their nominated family members prior to document ex-piration, ensuring timely renewals. From a business perspective, the platform enables companies to leverage data from uploaded documents to offer targeted, content-driven recommendations for products and brands. With its intuitive user interface and robust back-end infrastructure, the app delivers a comprehensive system for document management and expiry tracking, effectively meeting the diverse requirements of both individual users and businesses.

articleTitle: Enhancing Secure Medical Image Transmission Using Visually Meaningful Medical Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Medical images are transmitted to the remote location in a secure manner using medical image encryption. Conventional medical image encryption generates an unfamiliar image format that looks like noise or texture structure, which shows that the encrypted medical image contains secret information. Hence, the attacker aware of the visual existence of the secret image. To safeguard the visual appearance of the encrypted image, this paper proposed a visually meaningful medical image encryption based on Substitution and Permutation Network (SPN) structure. Performance analysis shows that the proposed methodology performs exceptionally well with various performance measures are considered.

articleTitle: Optimized-ANN for Predicting Cancer Using Gene Expression RNA-Seq Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Early detection of cancer is important because it can greatly enhance the likelihood of effective treatment and cure. Researchers have developed numerous approaches based on gene expression for cancer detection. Gene expression is the method by which Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid (DNA) is transformed to Ribose Nucleic Acid (RNA), and then to protein. Several strategies are available in the literature for the classification of cancerous and noncancerous genes from gene expression data. The current study investigates the performance of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) to predict the cancer type on a publicly available UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository. This study provides a comparative analysis of different extensions of Adam optimizers like Adaptive Moment (Adam), Adaptive Gradient (AdaGrad), as well as Nesterov-accelerated Adaptive Moment Estimation (Nadam) and proposes the significance of optimized ANNs in the form of a computationally efficient model. The study also explores the impact of multiple learning and decay rates on the prediction performance of ANN.

articleTitle: Distributed Brute-Force Password Recovery with a Partitioned Quantum Grover's Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: In the booming field of quantum computing, Grover's Algorithm emerges as a pivotal quantum search algorithm, theoretically capable of outperforming classical brute-force search methods by exploiting the principles of superposition and quantum parallelism. However, the practical application of Grover's Algorithm to crack complex passwords is limited by the nascent stage of quantum technology, which is currently challenged by limitations in qubit count and coherence times. This paper proposes a novel distributed quantum computing framework that aims to circumvent these limitations by partitioning the search space for a complex password among an array of quantum processors. Each processor executes Grover's Algorithm on a fraction of the total search space, thereby reducing the complexity and quantum resource requirements for each individual computation. The partial results are then transmitted to a central classical computer, which synthesizes them into the final password. This distributed approach not only makes the task feasible for (with) present-day quantum systems but also presents a scalable model that could adapt to the rapid advancements in quantum technologies. By dissecting the complexity of the quantum brute-force problem into smaller, more manageable units, this method holds the potential to significantly reduce the time complexity of password recovery processes and thus presents a profound progress (implications) for the fields of cryptography and cybersecurity.

articleTitle: GNN as Explainable Tool with Heterogeneous and Homogeneous Data for Medical Claim Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: This paper investigates the explainability of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in detecting fraudulent medical insurance claims, a critical challenge in the healthcare industry. Given the complexity of healthcare data and the high stakes involved in fraud detection, understanding model decisions is essential. We apply explainability techniques, GNNExplainer and PGExplainer to two GNN architectures: HINormer, a heterogeneous GNN, and RE-GraphSAGE, a modified homogeneous GNN adapted for heterogeneous data. Both models achieved high classification accuracy (84 % and 83 %) and served as a basis for evaluating the reliability and practicality of explainability techniques in health-care fraud detection, marking a pioneering effort in applying these methods to heterogeneous GNNs in medical claims. Using real-world data from the MENA region, we assess the ability of these explainers to provide meaningful interpretations of model decisions. Real-case scenarios reviewed by medical experts highlight that while these techniques can sometimes offer valid justifications, further development is required to ensure consistent reliability in practical settings. This work underscores the critical need for advanced explainability tools to foster trust and transparency in high-stakes medical decision-making.

articleTitle: WanderGenie: A Smart Guide for Immersive Tourism through Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Tourism encourages cultural interaction, economic growth, and global connectivity, improving both travelers and host communities. Due to the shortage of accessible and compe-tent guides, travelers often miss out on the rich history and cultural value of the areas they visit, leading to a shallow understanding of these sites. To bridge this knowledge gap, this article proposes WanderGenie: A Smart Guide for Immersive Tourism through Generative AI to enhance the visitor experience at popular places where traditional guides are unavailable. The system leverages image processing and RFID technology to recognize landmarks and provide travelers with real-time as well as detailed information about the spots they visit. The system ensures accurate landmark identification by strategically inserting RFID tags at precise spots. Upon detecting a landmark, the system shows relevant content through visual displays and audio outputs, creating an immersive and participatory experience. Acting as a kind virtual assistant, WanderGenie answers tourist's queries, improving their understanding and appreciation of the attractions they experience by utilizing Generative AI technology. This concept solves the shortage of guides while raising the qual-ity of the tourist experience by making historical, cultural, and architectural knowledge more accessible. The proposed system has been designed, implemented, and validated successfully.

articleTitle: Transforming IoT with Scalable Serverless Architecture for Enhanced Data Collection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Article explores the development and implementation of an IoT application utilizing Azure Functions, focusing on creating a scalable and efficient system for real-time data processing. The work integrates Azure Functions with a React-based web application, offering a practical approach to building robust IoT solutions using serverless architecture. A comprehensive analysis of various serverless platforms, including Microsoft Azure, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Functions, is provided, highlighting their advantages. The implementation phase demonstrates the effective use of Azure Functions and CosmosDB to gather and process data from IoT devices. The results showcase the potential of serverless computing in developing modern, scalable, and cost-effective IoT applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Beach Debris Collection and Segregation System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Marine debris has become a global problem, concerning all marine ecosystems, and humans alike. It's known to cause severe damage to the marine and coastal habitats, since a part of it washes up along the shores and reefs, and the remaining is swept off the coast leading to the sinking and persisting of the debris in the form of sediments for years. This submerged marine garbage contains items such as microplastics, large plastic fragments, fishing strings/nets, organic waste, and a lot more. Accumulation of such debris causes damage to the ecosystem, damaging the livelihood of all effected aquatic species, and also the people around these waters, as the microplastics in such waters is ingested by the fish, eventually making its way up the food chain. The motivation for building this project arose from the need to address the adverse effects of introducing trash into our marine ecosystems around the globe, and its detrimental impact on the ecosystem and beaches. To overcome these issues, we introduce the beach cleaning robot, an innovation in artificial intelligence and robotics. This bot improves upon an existing idea Bebot, thriving to provide better results in a more cost effective and easy-to-use manner. By using mapping technology and sensor detection techniques, this approach aims to pick up the trash from our beaches and coasts before it is washed out by the tides, helping us to cut down the amount of marine debris that makes it into the oceans from these sources. The final product will be a machine capable of distinguishing various types of waste that it collects, and segregating it into metallic and not metallic, cleaning the beach it is deployed at autonomously and providing long-term sustainability against beach debris. We envision a world where deploying such machines will not only result in cleaner beaches but also preserve the marine life in the surrounding area, allowing future generations to experience the beauty we enjoy right now.

articleTitle: Rotation-Invariant Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: This paper describes a self supervised representation learning approach that can perform robust object detection in out-of-distribution rotated images for autonomous driving task. Keeping in mind the limitations of vehicle sensors we incorporate self-supervised rotation invariance for correcting rotational corruptions. We present a comprehensive analysis of observed label shifts, validate the results using holdout sets and provide explainability for the performance uisng GradCAM appaorach. We demonstrate results on real-world adversarial examples: (Autonomous Scenes - DAWN dataset) that signifi-cantly outperform common methods. The proposed framework outperforms the rotation-affected benchmark by 14.73 points of mAP for the OD task in autonomous driving applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Class Grouping and Relabelling on Defect Detection in Solar Panels using YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: The use of solar panels is increasing rapidly globally, emphasizing the need of effective monitoring and maintenance strategies. This can be achieved by detecting and resolving the problems as early as possible to maintain high energy generation. Computer vision techniques have proven to be effective in this regard. Most of the conventional defect detection methods are inefficient to deal with multiple classes of defects, thereby delaying the response to address the problems. This study aims to fill in this gap using an efficient computer vision model, you only look once (YOLO) v9, to determine the impact of grouping defect classes on performance of solar panel defect detection models. The original six classes are grouped into three and two classes, respectively, using modified dataset and weighted average modes. Class grouping as well as the grouping methodology significantly impacts the performance of the model. The modified dataset method of class grouping performing better. The mean average precision at threshold 50% (mAP50) for 2-class grouping is 80.2%, which surpasses grouping into three classes by 3.2% and the original six-class setup by 5.6%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Alzheimer's Disease Detection: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques with Transfer Learning and Custom CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurological disorder that primarily impacts memory, cognition, and behavior, making it the leading cause of dementia in older adults. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and management. This study explores the application of deep learning methods to detect Alzheimer's disease using a dataset of 12,000 medical images, divided into four groups of 3,000 each. The images underwent processing with Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) to identify key features. Various machine learning techniques were applied, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Standard Scaling, and Stratified K-Fold cross-validation, to enhance the analysis across four algorithms. For the deep learning approach, we employed data augmentation and developed a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which achieved an accuracy of 89%. However, utilizing transfer learning with the VGG16 model significantly improved performance, reaching an accuracy of 94%. This comparative study highlights the superiority of the VGG16 model over the custom CNN for detecting Alzheimer's disease in medical images, emphasizing the transformative potential of advanced deep learning techniques, especially those leveraging transfer learning, in enhancing diagnostic accuracy for this condition.

articleTitle: Autoencoder and Multi-Head Attention with GRU based Approach to Predict Disease Outbreak using News-Crawl 2019 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Predicting disease outbreaks from news headlines is still challenging, as predictions rely on particular disease news data such as Ebola, Zika, SARS, MERS, COVID-19, and many more. A combined approach has been presented in this research work, where an Autoencoder and Multi-Head Attention combined with GRU used to predict disease outbreak. This work utilizes the News-Crawl 2019 data, where generic keywords are used to extract disease outbreak news headlines to predict whether or not news headlines are related to disease outbreaks. The work gains significance as the prediction is done without any bias, i.e., without being specific to the names of the disease to be predicted. The proposed approach achieves good accuracy on the test data through performance evaluation and has the capability to predict any disease outbreak, rather than just specific disease outbreaks, from news data. Whereas the combination of Autoencoder and Multi-Head Attention with GRU achieves 97.96% accuracy on test data.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Analog, Digital, and Hybrid Beamforming Techniques for Enhanced MIMO Wireless Communication Systems: Radiation Pattern and Normalized Power
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Beamforming approch is the essential for improving the efficiency of wireless communication networks. These approaches includes analog, digital and hybrid beamforming. Each approach offers unique advantages and presents specific challenges. Analog Beamforming is stands for its simplicity and cost-effectiveness, yet it has limited versatility. On the other side, Digital Beamforming offers greater flexibility at a higher expense and complexity. Hybrid Beamforming emerges as a balanced strategy that combines the benefits of both analog and digital approaches to improve performance, cost, and complexity. This study fully investigates the radiation patterns and normalized power characteristics of these three beamforming techniques. These findings underscore beamforming's capacity to enhance wireless communication and offer critical insights for augmenting the reliability and efficiency of wireless networks.

articleTitle: Optimized CNN Techniques for Intrusion Detection Using NBA-IoT Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Network Systems (CINS)
abstract: Over the past 15 years, the proliferation of Internet-connected devices due to the development of high-speed wireless communication technology has raised concerns about cybersecurity. As IoT (Internet of Things) technology penetrates every aspect of society, the potential damage from IoT cyberattacks is much greater than that from existing cyberattacks. Objective: The main goal of this study is to address the growing concerns about cybersecurity in the rapidly evolving Internet of Things (IoT) environment. As the number of Internet-connected devices increases, the potential damage from IoT hacking has become a major concern. Existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) have been found to be insufficient to protect IoT networks, and research on more effective defenses is needed. The objective of this project is to study the effectiveness of an intrusion detection system specifically designed for Internet of Things communication networks.
